reason: README quickstart shows tokenizer and text generation with Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base (~1.2GB, ungated), feasible on CPU.
demo: README 快速体验: 使用 tokenizer and 文本生成 (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base)
goal: Get the PaddleFormers README quickstart working on CPU only: install paddleformers (CPU PaddlePaddle) so that AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base') encodes '中华人民共和国' to [105492, 104773], and AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-Base', dtype='bfloat16').eval().generate(...) on the prompt '请给我一段大模型的简短介绍：' produces decoded text. The 'python' from /work/env.sh must be able to import paddleformers and paddle.
check: The hidden test runs the README tokenizer and text-generation snippets and verifies the expected token ids and that the model generates a sensible Chinese continuation (including a simple factual completion).

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Oracle content check is too lenient: it only requires the decoded generation to be longer than the prompt + 3 chars, so garbage output (e.g. a broken dtype fallback emitting repeated tokens) passes. v2 adds a CJK-content check on the README generation and a greedy factual completion ('中华人民共和国的首都是' -> contains '北京') via the documented decode_strategy kwarg.

Check text says the generated text 'extends the prompt', but generate() returns only the new tokens (the README snippet decodes outputs[0]); this misled the probe (the run explicitly worried about it). Check reworded.
evidence: oracles/paddlepaddle-paddleformers.sh:24-28 - only a length check on the decoded text
data/runs/paddlepaddle-paddleformers/result.json repair.final - 'generate returns only the new tokens, not the prompt'
